newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SMALL RETURNS AS SPRINGBOKS RING CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMALL RETURNS AS SPRINGBOKS RING CHANGES.

text.p: South Africa's most capped player James Small returns to make his 41st test appearance in the Tri-Nations match against New Zealand in Auckland on Saturday.

The recall of Small, who came on as fullback replacement during South Africa's 32-20 defeat by Australia in Brisbane on Saturday, was one of four changes made by coach Carel du Plessis in a bid to avoid a tournament whitewash.
He takes over the right wing position from Northern Transvaal flyer Andre Snyman who has been switched to the left wing in place of the demoted Pieter Rossouw.
Henry Honiball, who began the season at flyhalf, comes in at inside centre for the injured Danie van Schalkwyk and hooker Naka Drotske makes way for James Dalton.
Tighthead prop Marius Hurter, who missed Saturday's game because of influenza, was also recalled in place of Dawie Theron.
Veteran World Cup fullback Andre Joubert was also tipped for a recall after an erratic display by Russell Bennett against the Wallabies.
But du Plessis has resisted that temptation and has instead summoned the uncapped utility back Joe Gillingham to join the party following van Schalkwyk's broken ankle.
"Before selecting his side, Carel inquired about the fitness and performance of a number of players including Andre Joubert," South African media liaison officer Hermann Coetzee said.
"He eventually decided on Joe Gillingham because Joe can also play in the midfield which is an area that needed strengthening."
South Africa have lost both of their games in the Tri-Nations.

South Africa: 15-Russell Bennett; 14-James Small, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Henry Honiball, 11-Andre Snyman; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Marius Hurter, 2-James Dalton, 1-Os du Randt.
